clue.text: Liberal, worried, retreating along with others

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the combined letters are read from right to left

parts.note: ate, as in 'what's eating you', means worried or troubled

explanation.surface: A worried Liberal politician backs off alongside colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns LATE round to give the Latin abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin abbreviation et al. (et alii) is used in citations to mean 'and others'.

clue.text: What's said to be grief's early periods

indicators.note: what is said to be signals that the clue word is heard rather than spelt, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: grief's periods are times of mourning, so grief's gives mournings

explanation.surface: A meditation on the stages of grieving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grief's' does double duty with 'periods': grief's periods are mournings, which sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The first hours of each day are its earliest periods, from dawn till noon.

clue.text: Tense British military commander ignoring Grand National

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so a letter is dropped from the commander's name

parts.note: Douglas Haig commanded the British army on the Western Front in the First World War
G is the abbreviation for grand, slang for a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A nervous British general sits out the Grand National, Britain's famous steeplechase horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand National' looks like the horse race, but 'Grand' gives G and 'National' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Thailand is a Thai, a national of that country.

clue.text: Receptacle ex-PM breaks in a minute

indicators.note: breaks means forces its way into, so the former leader goes inside the other piece

parts.note: in a minute means shortly, soon
William Pitt (Elder or Younger) was a British prime minister

explanation.surface: A former prime minister smashes a container within sixty seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: A spittoon is a bowl-like vessel provided for spitting into.

clue.text: See 7
Accomplished Tory has problem with crony

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, the Tory party
a sum is an arithmetic problem
a mate is a pal or crony

explanation.surface: A skilled Conservative politician struggles with a dubious associate.
explanation.definitionFit: Consummate as an adjective means supremely skilled, perfect, highly accomplished.

clue.text: With onset of nineties, memories not working could result in one

definitions.text: With onset of nineties, memories not working could result in one

indicators.note: working here means being worked into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged
onset of means the start, so only the opening letter of nineties is taken

explanation.surface: Reaching ninety with a failing memory may bring on a lapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not working' looks like the anagram signal, but 'not' is part of the fodder and 'working' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior moment is a brief lapse of memory, jokingly attributed to old age, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Shoe that's 11 9

parts.note: 11 9 is LONG IN THE TOOTH, read as instructions: the first letter of long placed in a cog, a gear tooth

explanation.surface: An elderly piece of footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is read literally: L (from LONG) goes IN THE TOOTH, a COG, giving the wooden shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A clog is a heavy shoe with a wooden sole, an old-fashioned type of footwear.

clue.text: See 11
Electricity generator nicked in post office — thief may end up here!

indicators.note: in shows the stolen goods placed inside the post office abbreviation

parts.note: hot means stolen, nicked in British slang
a convicted thief may end up in a prison cell

explanation.surface: A thief steals power equipment from a post office and lands in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nicked' is British slang for stolen, and also for arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: A photoelectric cell produces electric current from light falling on it.

clue.text: Old, hot neon light to burst

indicators.note: burst means broken apart, so the letters fly into a new order

explanation.surface: An ageing hot neon tube is about to explode.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from judging a horse's age by its teeth, means getting old.

clue.text: Singer's a scam and a pain

definitions.meaning: the rock musician of The Police, Gordon Sumner, performs under this stage name
a confidence trick or police set-up operation
a sharp smarting hurt, as from an insect

explanation.surface: A performer is called a fraud and an annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a famous rock vocalist, a con or entrapment operation, and a sharp prickling hurt.

clue.text: Opener from 13 down to goad: 11 9? 27? 24 required!

definitions.text: Opener from 13 down to goad: 11 9? 27? 24 required!

indicators.note: opener from means the first letter of the singer-poet's name

parts.note: 13 down is the poet, Dylan Thomas, sharing a name with the singer

indicators.note: 24 down is RAGING, which signals that the letters rage about into a new order

parts.note: 11 9 is the phrase meaning old, long in the tooth
27 across is the phrase meaning ageing, getting on

explanation.surface: Dylan Thomas's famous opening line urges the old to rage against dying.
explanation.walkthrough: The poem's opening line is also its title and refrain; the cross-referenced RAGING echoes its 'Rage, rage against the dying of the light'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the first line of Dylan Thomas's villanelle urging his ageing father to fight death.

clue.text: Singer's body language somewhat lacking

indicators.note: somewhat lacking says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A performer's gestures are rather poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Dylan is the American singer-songwriter; the 's means 'is'.

clue.text: Disagreeable poster sending up the antiquated, mostly broken public transport

parts.note: a troll is someone who posts provocative messages online

indicators.note: sending up in a down entry means writing the letters from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: ye is the mock-old form of 'the', as in Ye Olde Shoppe

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: bust means broken

explanation.surface: An unpleasant internet commenter mocks a creaky, broken-down bus service.
explanation.definitionFit: A trolleybus is an electric bus drawing power from overhead wires, a form of public transport.

clue.text: Hurt one invading brown monkey

indicators.note: invading means going into, so these pieces sit inside the colour

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
to mar is to damage or hurt
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An injured creature intrudes on a brown primate.
explanation.definitionFit: A tamarin is a small South American primate related to marmosets.

clue.text: See 13 across
Girl with love for bondage apparatus

parts.note: lass is a girl, especially in northern England and Scotland
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A woman and her partner shop for restraints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bondage apparatus' suggests something kinky; it is a rope for binding cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a looped rope used to catch and tie up animals, a tool for binding.

clue.text: Boycott about to make catch

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a ban is a boycott or embargo

explanation.surface: The cricketer Geoffrey Boycott is about to take a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Boycott was an English cricketer, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: To nab is to seize or grab, as in catching a ball or a criminal.

clue.text: Dressed lobster with a fish

indicators.note: dressed, as in preparing seafood, means the letters are worked over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A seafood platter of dressed lobster with a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloaters are herrings cured by salting and light smoking, so they are fish.

clue.text: Type of suit for flier given onus for wintery Shakespearean role

indicators.note: the answer given an added word becomes the role, so that word is taken off the role to leave it

parts.note: Antigonus is a lord in The Winter's Tale, famous for exiting pursued by a bear
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pilot's suit is weighed down with responsibility for a part in a winter play.
explanation.walkthrough: A subtraction: the answer plus ONUS makes ANTIGONUS, so the role loses ONUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti-g suit is a pressurised garment worn by pilots to resist gravity forces.

clue.text: See 13 across
Nag runs after horse reportedly stuck in river

indicators.note: after places the runs abbreviation behind the river piece, so it comes last
stuck in means placed inside, so the horse goes inside the river

parts.note: the Nile is the great African river

indicators.note: reportedly means as it sounds, so the spoken form of the horse is written as letters

parts.note: gee-gee is a childish word for horse, said like the letters GG
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A tired old horse comes in after another, stuck in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' looks like a horse, beside 'horse', but it is the definition: a person who nags.
explanation.definitionFit: A niggler is someone who keeps finding fault or complaining, a carping nag.

clue.text: See 13 across
Romeo 11 9, like The Tempest?

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
11 9 is LONG IN THE TOOTH, which means growing old

explanation.surface: Romeo grows old, as in a stormy Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitalised 'The Tempest' points to Shakespeare's play, but the definition wants a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent storm, which is furious and wild, like a raging sea.

clue.text: Ham and egg girl cut, removing filling

parts.note: an egg is O-shaped, so egg gives O
Vera is a girl's name

indicators.note: removing filling means the inner letter is taken out

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A breakfast order of ham and egg, with the girl trimming the sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham and egg' reads like breakfast; 'Ham' is the verb-like definition, a poor actor's style.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to perform in an exaggerated, theatrical way, which is what overacting means.

clue.text: Excited to get tips from revolutionary

parts.note: the tips, or end letters, of the word revolutionary are ..., spelt out as a phrase

explanation.surface: A rebel's inside information gets someone worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: The end letters of 'revolutionary' are R and Y; written out as 'R and Y' they make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Randy is British slang for lustful or sexually aroused, a kind of excitement.

clue.text: Fleece jumper put on king

indicators.note: put on in a down clue means placed above, so the jumper comes first

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumper
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A woolly sweater is pulled on over the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleece' and 'jumper' look like clothing, but jumper is the kangaroo and Fleece is to swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook is to cheat or swindle someone out of money, as to fleece does.

clue.text: Coping with being 11 9

definitions.meaning: 11 9 means old, so this sense is growing old

explanation.surface: Managing as one ages.
explanation.walkthrough: A double definition: one sense is managing, the other is growing old.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both managing or progressing and becoming elderly.

clue.text: See 13 across
Turn back for nibbles

indicators.note: back means read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a spin is a turn or rotation

explanation.surface: Turning around to snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Nips are small bites, like nibbles.

clue.text: Black vessel in painting, queen's ship

parts.note: an oil is an oil painting
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an urn is a vase-like vessel
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A painting shows a dark pot, and the Queen's ship.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil-burner can be a ship fuelled by oil, though it is better known as a heating unit.

clue.text: Hamlet once giving deity power

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: Prince Hamlet once told of a god who gave him strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' suggests Shakespeare's prince; here it is a small village, and 'once' marks an old word.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorp is an archaic word for a small village, found in English place names.
